title: Final Capital Variants — 4-Component Confirmed Portfolio
note_sharedVsSeparateFDXS: summary.json uses 1×FDXS shared (margin €3,902). Separate FDXS (2×) gives total €4,782. Capital pass thresholds differ accordingly. Both scenarios documented below.

kpis_from_summary.note: KPIs are reference values from best variant at this capital — not live-tradeable at this level

scenario_sharedFDXS.caveat: Operational risk: if DAX1H and DAX2H trigger simultaneously, 2nd FDXS contract needed. Shared FDXS creates execution risk.
scenario_sharedFDXS.note: PASS with shared FDXS — lowest compliant level for this scenario

scenario_separateFDXS.note: PASS — lowest compliant level for separate FDXS scenario

kpis_from_summary.note: Best risk-adjusted profile in the table. Recommended minimum for operational deployment.

recommendation.rationale: €20k passes 30% margin rule with separate FDXS. €30k provides meaningful drawdown buffer (at 7.4% MaxDD on €20k capital, worst drawdown = ~€1,480; at €30k that same DD is 4.9% of capital — more comfortable psychologically and operationally).
recommendation.alphaNote: Higher capital reduces cost drag proportionally but reduces return-on-capital. The €20k level offers the best balance of margin safety, cost efficiency, and return potential for a 4-component starter portfolio.
recommendation.wfSummary: 9/9 folds positive for all confirmed variants. OOS/IS ratio 1.40-1.48 (not overfitted). Cost-stress ×1.5 remains positive. Highest quality WF gate in the system.
